subject: Physics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Kinematics Conceptual Ontology, First-Move Atlas & Subtopic Competencies

stage_1_choose.name: Spatial-Temporal Invariant & Origin Setup
stage_1_choose.action: Declare spatial origin x = 0 (or launch level y = 0), define positive coordinate direction (+), and synchronize clock zero t = 0.
stage_1_choose.invariant: Physical events (collisions, turning points, apex heights) are strictly invariant under choice of origin.

stage_2_represent.name: Dual Kinematic Representation
stage_2_represent.action: Construct UVATS 5-parameter state table, signed number line, or motion graph (x-t / v-t) capturing phase boundaries.
stage_2_represent.invariant: Boundary state continuity: final velocity and position of phase k form the exact initial state of phase k+1.

stage_3_connect.name: Kinematic Quad & Decoupled Invariants
stage_3_connect.action: Select the unique kinematic equation eliminating the unmeasured variable, or decouple orthogonal 2D components.
stage_3_connect.invariant: Constant-acceleration equations apply IF AND ONLY IF da/dt = 0; perpendicular axes share only scalar time t.

stage_4_execute_and_check.name: Algebraic Execution & Limiting Boundary Verification
stage_4_execute_and_check.action: Solve closed-form algebraic expressions and verify asymptotic limits (a -> 0, g -> 0, t -> 0) and dimensional homogeneity.
stage_4_execute_and_check.invariant: All distance/displacement formulas must have dimension [L]; speeds [L T^-1]; accelerations [L T^-2].

structural_pillars.name: Spatial-Temporal Coordinate Invariance
structural_pillars.principle: Kinematic trajectories and physical intervals are invariant under translation of spatial origin and clock zero.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: Delta x = x_f - x_i; Delta t = t_f - t_i

structural_pillars.name: Geometric Calculus Slope-Area Duality
structural_pillars.principle: Differentiation yields instantaneous rates (slope); integration accumulates physical displacement and velocity changes (area).
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: v(t) = dx/dt, a(t) = dv/dt; Delta x = int v dt, Delta v = int a dt

structural_pillars.name: Kinematic Quad & Uniform Acceleration Constraint
structural_pillars.principle: The four standard kinematic equations are mathematically exact if and only if acceleration is strictly time-invariant.

structural_pillars.name: Directional Sign Consistency & Inversion Dynamics
structural_pillars.principle: Vectors along 1D axes are signed scalars. Speed magnitude |v| increases when v and a share signs; turnaround occurs at v = 0.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: d|v|/dt > 0 <=> sgn(v) == sgn(a); v_turn = 0 with a != 0

structural_pillars.name: Galilean Invariance & Relative Frame Transformation
structural_pillars.principle: Under uniform gravity, relative acceleration between free bodies vanishes identically, rectifying relative trajectories into straight lines.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: a_rel = a_A - a_B = 0 => v_rel = const; r_rel(t) = r_rel,0 + v_rel*t

KIN-01.title: Distance vs Displacement Invariant
KIN-01.definition: Distinction between scalar cumulative path length and vector net endpoint change on a signed 1D axis.
canonical_rules: Displacement Delta x = x_f - x_i depends strictly on start and finish positions.
Distance s = sum |Delta x_k| accumulates all forward and backward leg lengths.
|Delta x| <= distance s, with equality holding if and only if motion is unidirectional without reversal.
operational_heuristics: Mark start, turn, and finish on one signed number line.
Never convert signed displacement legs into absolute values prior to algebraic addition.
boundary_conditions: Unidirectional motion: |Delta x| = s.
Closed round trip: Delta x = 0 while s = 2L > 0.

KIN-02.title: Average Speed vs Average Velocity
KIN-02.definition: Ratio of total displacement vs total distance to total elapsed clock time.
canonical_rules: Average velocity v_avg = Delta x / Delta t.
Average speed s_avg = (total distance) / Delta t.
On any closed round trip, average velocity is identically zero while average speed is strictly positive.
operational_heuristics: Calculate total elapsed clock time Delta t_tot = sum t_k before forming any quotient.
Instantaneous velocity is the limiting derivative v = dx/dt as Delta t -> 0.
boundary_conditions: Round trip: v_avg = 0, s_avg = 2d / (t1 + t2).
Uniform speed motion: s_avg = |v_avg|.

KIN-03.title: Weighted Kinematic Averages
KIN-03.definition: Mathematical formulation of average speed over partitioned intervals with equal-time versus equal-distance weighting.
canonical_rules: Equal-time intervals yield arithmetic mean: v_avg = (v1 + v2) / 2.
Equal-distance intervals yield harmonic mean: v_avg = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2).
Harmonic mean is strictly less than arithmetic mean for distinct positive speeds (v1 != v2).
operational_heuristics: Identify the equal parameter: if equal distance, longer time is spent at slower speed, pulling the average down.
Never apply arithmetic average to equal-distance travel legs.
boundary_conditions: v1 = v2 = v: v_avg = v.
v2 -> 0 on second half: v_avg -> 0 (trip never completes).
v2 -> infinity: v_avg -> 2*v1 (bounded by twice the slower speed).

KIN-04.title: Signs, Direction & Acceleration Reversal
KIN-04.definition: Interpretation of algebraic signs of velocity and acceleration along a chosen 1D axis.
canonical_rules: Sign of velocity determines direction of motion (+x or -x).
Sign of acceleration determines direction of velocity vector change (dv/dt).
Speeding up occurs when v and a have identical signs; slowing down occurs when v and a have opposite signs.
operational_heuristics: Negative acceleration speeds up a body traveling in the negative direction.
Turnaround instant occurs where v = 0; acceleration can remain constant and non-zero across the turnaround.
boundary_conditions: v > 0, a > 0: speeding up in +x direction.
v < 0, a < 0: speeding up in -x direction.
v > 0, a < 0: slowing down in +x direction prior to reversal.

KIN-05.title: Constant Acceleration Equation Selection
KIN-05.definition: Systematic selection and execution of the kinematic quad under uniform acceleration.
canonical_rules: The kinematic quad is valid IF AND ONLY IF acceleration is constant (da/dt = 0).
v = u + at (omits displacement s).
s = ut + 0.5*a*t^2 (omits final velocity v).
v^2 = u^2 + 2as (omits elapsed time t).
s = 0.5*(u + v)*t (omits acceleration a).
operational_heuristics: Build UVATS state table: list {u, v, a, t, s}, identify the unknown target, and pick the equation omitting the 5th variable.
boundary_conditions: a = 0: recovers uniform motion s = ut, v = u.

KIN-06.title: Multiphase & Delayed-Start Motion
KIN-06.definition: Partitioning piecewise uniform motions and handling staggered clocks across multiple bodies.
canonical_rules: Final velocity and position of phase k constitute initial state of phase k+1.
Delayed start: if body B starts at clock time t_delay, elapsed time for B is tau = t - t_delay (tau >= 0).
Displacement in n-th second: s_n = u + 0.5*a*(2n - 1).
operational_heuristics: Reset local clock for each phase while carrying forward physical state variables.
Set position functions equal x_A(t) = x_B(t) to solve catch-up / collision conditions.
boundary_conditions: t < t_delay: body B remains stationary at starting position.
Catch-up condition: x_A(t) = x_B(t) must have real positive root t >= t_delay.

KIN-07.title: Vertical Free Fall & Apex Invariants
KIN-07.definition: 1D motion under constant gravitational acceleration a_y = -g in vacuum.
canonical_rules: Acceleration is strictly a_y = -g throughout ascent, apex, and descent.
At apex summit, instantaneous velocity vanishes (v_y = 0) while acceleration remains exactly -g.
Time of ascent equals time of descent to launch level: t_up = t_down = u / g.
Maximum height reached: H_max = u^2 / (2g).
operational_heuristics: Never set acceleration to zero at the apex.
Use time-reversal symmetry: descent from apex is identical to release from rest.
boundary_conditions: y = H_max: v = 0, a = -g.
Return to launch level: y = 0, t = 2u/g, v = -u.

KIN-08.title: 2D Projectile Component Decoupling
KIN-08.definition: Orthogonal decomposition of 2D planar motion into independent 1D kinematic components.
canonical_rules: Perpendicular motions (x and y) are completely independent and share only clock time t.
Horizontal motion is uniform: a_x = 0, v_x = u cos theta, x(t) = (u cos theta)*t.
Vertical motion is uniform free fall: a_y = -g, v_y = u sin theta - gt, y(t) = (u sin theta)*t - 0.5*g*t^2.
operational_heuristics: Horizontal launch speed has zero influence on vertical drop time.
Solve for time t from vertical equation and substitute into horizontal equation.
boundary_conditions: Horizontal launch (theta = 0): v_x = u, v_y = -gt, t_fall = sqrt(2h/g).
Landing on level ground: y(T) = 0 => T = 2u sin theta / g.

KIN-09.title: Projectile Trajectory & Flight Landmarks
KIN-09.definition: Mathematical formulation of parabolic trajectory, horizontal range, and elevation envelope.
canonical_rules: Trajectory is a Cartesian parabola: y(x) = x tan theta - (g / (2*u^2*cos^2 theta)) * x^2.
Horizontal range on level ground: R = (u^2 sin 2theta) / g.
Complementary launch angles (theta and 90 deg - theta) produce identical horizontal ranges at equal launch speeds.
Maximum horizontal range occurs at theta = 45 deg: R_max = u^2 / g.
operational_heuristics: Symmetric range formula applies ONLY when launch height equals landing height.
For cliff launch, determine flight time from quadratic equation in y(t) = -h.
boundary_conditions: theta = 45 deg: R = R_max = u^2/g, H = R_max / 4.
theta = 90 deg: R = 0, pure vertical motion recovered.

KIN-10.title: Relative Velocity & Common Acceleration Cancellation
KIN-10.definition: Classical Galilean relative motion and cancellation of uniform gravitational acceleration.
canonical_rules: Relative velocity: v_AB = v_A - v_B.
When two bodies experience identical acceleration (a_A = a_B = -g), relative acceleration is identically ZERO (a_rel = 0).
The relative trajectory of one freely falling projectile viewed from another is a uniform straight line.
operational_heuristics: Transform into the reference frame of one projectile to eliminate gravity completely.
Collision occurs if and only if relative velocity points directly along initial line-of-sight vector.
boundary_conditions: Identical launch velocities (u_A = u_B): v_rel = 0, separation distance remains constant forever.
Opposite colinear launch: relative approach speed is u_A + u_B.

KIN-11.title: Motion Graphs & Geometric Calculus
KIN-11.definition: Visual representation of kinematics through slope (derivative) and area (integral) duality.
canonical_rules: Slope of x-t graph is instantaneous velocity v = dx/dt; concavity is acceleration d^2x/dt^2.
Slope of v-t graph is instantaneous acceleration a = dv/dt.
Signed area under v-t curve represents net displacement Delta x = int v dt.
Absolute area under v-t curve represents cumulative distance s = int |v| dt.
Signed area under a-t curve represents change in velocity Delta v = v_f - v_i.
operational_heuristics: Vertical line test: an x-t graph cannot loop or intersect a vertical line twice (single-valued physical history).
A sharp corner in an x-t curve implies an infinite acceleration impulse.
boundary_conditions: Horizontal line on x-t: v = 0 (particle at rest).
Horizontal line on v-t: a = 0 (uniform motion).
Straight line on v-t: a = const (uniform acceleration).

first_move_atlas.cue: Reversing direction, turnaround instant, or zigzag path along a straight line
first_move_atlas.representation: Signed 1D number line with start point x_i, turning coordinates x_turn, and end point x_f clearly marked
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Write displacement Delta x = x_f - x_i; write distance s = sum |Delta x_k| by summing absolute segment lengths
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Converting signed leg displacements to absolute values before computing net displacement

first_move_atlas.cue: Complete round trip or returning to initial origin with known leg speeds
first_move_atlas.representation: Trajectory phase strip with individual segment times t_k = d_k / v_k and total clock Delta t_tot = sum t_k
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Immediately set net displacement Delta x = 0 to establish v_avg = 0; compute average speed s_avg = (total distance) / (total time)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Confusing average speed with average velocity magnitude on round trips where displacement vanishes

first_move_atlas.cue: Equal distance segments or equal time intervals covered at different uniform speeds v1 and v2
first_move_atlas.representation: Dual-segment diagram explicitly labeling equal interval variable (Delta t vs d) and calculating dependent parameter
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: For equal distances, write t_tot = d/v1 + d/v2 to deduce harmonic mean v_avg = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2); for equal times, write arithmetic mean (v1 + v2)/2
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Blindly computing the arithmetic mean (v1 + v2)/2 when equal distances are traversed

first_move_atlas.cue: Particle moving with negative velocity u < 0 or experiencing negative acceleration a < 0
first_move_atlas.representation: 1D coordinate axis with signed velocity and acceleration arrows placed at particle position
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Compare signs of v and a: if sgn(v) == sgn(a), the particle is speeding up; if sgn(v) != sgn(a), the particle is slowing down
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Equating negative acceleration directly to deceleration without checking the sign of velocity

first_move_atlas.cue: Uniform acceleration motion with one omitted or unrequested variable among {u, v, a, t, s}
first_move_atlas.representation: UVATS 5-parameter state table listing known values, target quantity, and the single excluded parameter
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Select the exact kinematic equation that omits the unrequested parameter (e.g., v^2 = u^2 + 2as when time t is unmentioned)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Solving multi-step quadratic systems for intermediate time t when a direct time-free equation exists

first_move_atlas.cue: Multi-phase piecewise acceleration, delayed vehicle launch, or distance in the n-th second
first_move_atlas.representation: Multi-segment timeline with boundary state continuity (v_1,end = u_2,start) and local clocks tau = t - t_delay
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Carry forward boundary speed as initial velocity for next phase; for n-th second, apply s_n = u + 0.5*a*(2n - 1)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Applying a single global kinematic formula across multiple distinct acceleration intervals

first_move_atlas.cue: Vertical toss under gravity, apex summit turnaround, or symmetrical free fall
first_move_atlas.representation: Vertical axis +y upward with a_y = -g labeled continuously at launch, apex, and descent
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Set vertical apex velocity v_top = 0 while preserving acceleration a_y = -g; apply v^2 = u^2 - 2gH to find H_max = u^2 / (2g)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Setting acceleration a = 0 at the highest point of flight where instantaneous velocity momentarily vanishes

first_move_atlas.cue: 2D projectile launched horizontally from elevated height or obliquely across level ground
first_move_atlas.representation: 2D Cartesian coordinate frame with independent 1D horizontal (a_x = 0) and vertical (a_y = -g) projections
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Decouple into independent motions: x(t) = (u cos theta)*t and y(t) = (u sin theta)*t - 0.5*g*t^2, linked strictly by clock t
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Believing horizontal velocity influences the vertical time of fall or gravitational acceleration

first_move_atlas.cue: Parabolic trajectory equation, maximum range condition, or complementary launch angles
first_move_atlas.representation: Parabolic path sketch showing apex coordinates (R/2, H_max), range landing (R, 0), and velocity vector tangents
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Substitute t = x / (u cos theta) into y(t) to form trajectory equation y = x tan theta - g*x^2 / (2*u^2*cos^2 theta)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Using symmetric ground-to-ground range formula R = u^2 sin 2theta / g when launch and landing heights are unequal

first_move_atlas.cue: Two bodies in simultaneous flight under gravity or relative pursuit/interception
first_move_atlas.representation: Relative reference frame anchored on body B with relative position r_rel = r_A - r_B and relative velocity v_rel = v_A - v_B
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Notice common acceleration cancellation: a_rel = a_A - a_B = (-g) - (-g) = 0, reducing relative motion to a constant-velocity straight line
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Retaining gravitational acceleration terms in the relative trajectory equation of two freely falling projectiles

first_move_atlas.cue: Motion graphs (x-t, v-t, a-t), piecewise linear curves, or physical graph consistency checks
first_move_atlas.representation: Graph geometry inspection: identify curve tangent slope as derivative and signed area under curve as definite integral
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Extract physical rates: slope of x-t is v; slope of v-t is a; signed area under v-t is displacement Delta x; area under a-t is Delta v
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Confusing the vertical height coordinate of an x-t graph with the instantaneous speed of the particle

nodes.description: Declared spatial origin and clock setting zero coordinates (x0, t0).
Position coordinate x(t) vs cumulative scalar path length s = int |v| dt.
Net change in position coordinate: Delta x = x(t2) - x(t1).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When a vertically thrown projectile reaches its highest point (apex), its velocity is zero, so its acceleration must also be zero.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Velocity is zero momentarily at the turnaround instant, but acceleration is the derivative dv/dt = -g != 0. If acceleration were zero at the apex, the ball would remain suspended in mid-air indefinitely.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: High-speed strobe photography and accelerometer attached to a vertical toss reveal constant -9.8 m/s^2 readout continuously through the apex.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Total distance traveled is always equal to the magnitude of displacement.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Displacement is the net vector change in position Delta x. Distance is the cumulative path length. In any round-trip or reverse motion, distance > 0 while displacement = 0.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A runner on a 400 m circular track completes one full lap: odometer reads 400 m, but displacement from start to finish is exactly 0 m.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A car travelling half the distance at v1 and the remaining half at v2 has average speed (v1 + v2) / 2.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. For equal distances, the car spends more time at the slower speed, yielding the harmonic mean v_avg = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2). The arithmetic average applies only to equal time intervals.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Driving 60 km at 30 km/h (takes 2 hours) and 60 km at 60 km/h (takes 1 hour). Total distance = 120 km, total time = 3 hours => average speed = 40 km/h, not 45 km/h.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A bullet fired horizontally at 500 m/s will take longer to hit the ground than a bullet dropped simultaneously from the same height.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Horizontal and vertical motions decouple completely. Both bullets experience identical vertical acceleration a_y = -g with identical initial vertical velocity u_y = 0, hitting the ground simultaneously at t = sqrt(2h/g).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Classic physics apparatus: a spring-loaded launcher simultaneously shoots one ball horizontally while dropping a second ball vertically from the same height; audio sensors record a single simultaneous ground impact click.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.concept: Motion Graph Slope vs Height Conflation
cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: On a position-time graph, when the curve crosses the time axis (x = 0), the velocity is zero; or on a velocity-time graph, a negative velocity indicates deceleration.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: On an x-t graph, velocity is the tangent slope dx/dt, not position x(t). On a v-t graph, sign indicates direction of motion; deceleration occurs if and only if velocity and acceleration have opposite signs (|v| is decreasing).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A car passing through x = 0 at 100 km/h has zero position but high speed. A ball tossed upward has v < 0 and a < 0 on the downward leg, meaning it is accelerating downward (speeding up in the negative direction).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Two objects falling freely near Earth accelerate toward each other because gravity pulls both of them.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Because both objects experience the identical acceleration a = -g, their relative acceleration is a_rel = a_1 - a_2 = 0. In their relative frame, gravity is completely eliminated, and their relative motion is uniform constant velocity.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Releasing two stones from different heights inside an Einstein free-falling elevator: both hover at constant separation distance relative to the elevator and each other.
